Vyshnivets New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ternopilska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. This record shows a tension worth noting: it is categorized as 'fenced and protected,' yet the source's demolished field marks it as 'yes.' Vyshnivets's Jewish population peaked at 3,178 in 1847, supporting five synagogues and a Talmud-Torah by 1863. During the Russian Civil War, a Jewish self-defense group here successfully staved off violence — a notably effective outcome. Eight synagogues operated by the 1930s. Over 400 Jews were murdered soon after the German occupation in July 1941, and the ghetto's liquidation on August 11, 1942, saw about 2,500 people executed. This cemetery remained in operation until the beginning of the 21st century.
